newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: RESEARCH ALERT-Barings overweight on Colombia shrs.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Barings overweight on Colombia shrs.

text.p: ING Barings said it remains overweight in Colombia, a country where it sees strong market performance continuing through the end of the year.

"Colombia had the second-highest market performance in the region after Brazil last quarter because cheap valuations and low real interest rates brought on a return in investor confidence," Alejandra Torres, ING Barings' head of Colombia equity research, said in a statement.

"Colombia maintains one of the highest estimated index upsides in Latin America," the statement said, adding that both Bogota's IBB and Medellin's IBOMED general price index have "considerable long-term upside before they surpass their historical peaks of 1994.
"Colombia remains the region's cheapest market, with estimated 1997 and 1998 price/earnings ratios at 11.1 times and 9.8 times, respectively," it said.
It added that Barings' top five picks in Colombian stocks were Banco de Colombia, Cementos Argos, Exito, Carulla and Suramericana.

The statement said Colombia's economy was seen growing by 3.8 percent this year and 4.5 percent in 1998, but it stressed this was unlikely to affect corporate earnings significantly since growth would be "skewed toward natural resources and infrastructure sectors."
